title: CHAPTER 4: TISSUES – PLANT AND ANIMAL TISSUES

blocks.content: 1. Tissue – Definition

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Histology is the branch of science dedicated to the study of tissues.
Plant tissues are categorized into dividing Meristematic tissues and non-dividing Permanent tissues.
Simple permanent plant tissues include Parenchyma, Collenchyma, and dead Sclerenchyma cells.
Complex permanent tissues consist of Xylem (water conduction) and Phloem (food transport).
Animal tissues comprise Epithelial, Connective, Muscular, and Nervous tissues, with the neuron as the functional unit of nervous tissue.

blocks.content:
A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform a specific function.
These cells have a common origin, structure, and function.
The concept of tissue helps in understanding the organization of multicellular organisms.
In unicellular organisms, one cell performs all life functions, but in multicellular organisms, cells are specialized.
This specialization increases efficiency of work.
The study of tissues is called Histology.
Tissues combine to form organs, and organs form organ systems.
SSC often asks definition-based and concept-based questions from this topic.
2. Types of Tissues

Tissues are broadly classified into two main types: Plant tissues and Animal tissues.
Plant tissues help plants in growth, support, conduction, and protection.
Animal tissues help in movement, coordination, protection, and transport.
This classification is very important for SSC exams.
Questions are often asked on types and functions of tissues.
Understanding this classification forms the base for further topics.
3. Plant Tissues – Classification

Plant tissues are classified into two main types: Meristematic tissues and Permanent tissues.
Meristematic tissues are actively dividing tissues.
Permanent tissues are formed from meristematic tissues and lose the power of division.
Permanent tissues are further divided into simple and complex tissues.
This classification is frequently asked in SSC exams.
4. Meristematic Tissue

Meristematic tissue consists of actively dividing cells.
These tissues are responsible for the growth of plants.
Cells of meristematic tissue have dense cytoplasm, thin cell walls, and large nuclei.
They lack vacuoles.
Meristematic tissues are of three types: Apical, Intercalary, and Lateral.
Apical meristem increases length of plant.
Lateral meristem increases girth of plant.
Intercalary meristem is found at nodes.
These facts are important for SSC MCQs.
5. Permanent Tissue
Xylem transports water and minerals from roots to leaves.

Permanent tissues are formed from meristematic tissues.
They lose the ability to divide.
Permanent tissues are of two types: Simple permanent tissues and Complex permanent tissues.
Simple tissues are made of one type of cell.
Complex tissues are made of more than one type of cell.
Permanent tissues perform functions like storage, support, and transport.
6. Simple Permanent Tissues

Simple permanent tissues include Parenchyma, Collenchyma, and Sclerenchyma.
Parenchyma stores food and helps in photosynthesis.
Collenchyma provides flexibility and mechanical support.
Sclerenchyma provides strength and rigidity.
Cells of sclerenchyma are dead and have thick lignified walls.
SSC frequently asks differences between these tissues.
7. Complex Permanent Tissues

Complex permanent tissues include Xylem and Phloem.
Xylem transports water and minerals from roots to leaves.
Phloem transports food from leaves to other parts of the plant.
Xylem elements include tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma, and xylem fibres.
Phloem elements include sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, and phloem fibres.
These are highly important for SSC exams.

Transports food from leaves to other parts of the plant

blocks.content: 8. Animal Tissues – Classification

Animal tissues are classified into four main types: Epithelial, Connective, Muscular, and Nervous tissues.
Each tissue performs a specific function.
This classification is extremely important for SSC.
Direct questions are frequently asked from this topic.
9. Epithelial Tissue

Epithelial tissue covers body surfaces and lines internal organs.
It protects underlying tissues.
Epithelial tissue is of various types: Squamous, Cuboidal, Columnar, Ciliated, and Glandular.
Squamous epithelium forms lining of blood vessels.
Cuboidal epithelium is found in kidney tubules.
Columnar epithelium is found in intestine.
This tissue has no blood vessels.
SSC often asks location-based questions.
10. Connective Tissue

Connective tissue connects, supports, and binds other tissues.
It includes areolar tissue, adipose tissue, cartilage, bone, blood, and lymph.
Areolar tissue connects skin to muscles.
Adipose tissue stores fat.
Bone provides support and protection.
Blood transports oxygen and nutrients.
Lymph helps in immunity.
Functions and examples are important for SSC.
11. Muscular Tissue

items: Sclerenchyma cells are dead and feature thick lignified cell walls.
Blood, bone, adipose, and lymph are all classified as Connective Tissues.
Cardiac muscles are involuntary and located exclusively in the heart.
Apical meristem increases length, whereas Lateral meristem increases the girth of the plant.

blocks.content:
Muscular tissue is responsible for movement.
It consists of muscle fibres that contract and relax.
Muscular tissue is of three types: Skeletal, Smooth, and Cardiac.
Skeletal muscles are voluntary and attached to bones.
Smooth muscles are involuntary.
Cardiac muscles are found in heart only.
Differences between muscle types are frequently asked.
12. Nervous Tissue

Nervous tissue is specialized for conduction of nerve impulses.
It is found in brain, spinal cord, and nerves.
The functional unit of nervous tissue is neuron.
Neuron consists of dendrites, cell body, and axon.
This tissue helps in coordination and control.
SSC asks structure and function-based questions.
13. IMPORTANT FACTS – SSC FOCUS

• Study of tissues is called Histology.
• Meristematic tissues are actively dividing.
• Sclerenchyma cells are dead.
• Xylem transports water; Phloem transports food.
• Blood is a connective tissue.
• Cardiac muscles are involuntary.
• Squamous epithelium lines blood vessels.
• Nervous tissue conducts impulses.
• Adipose tissue stores fat.
• Bone is a connective tissue.
